How it works

One engine. Your business's rules.

Every business runs on the same proven setup — what changes is the knowledge file: your services, your prices, your calendar, your emergency rules.

01

We build your knowledge file

Your services, hours, pricing, service area, insurance or menu questions — everything your best front-desk person knows, written down once, with you approving every line.

02

It answers on both channels

Calls are picked up on the first ring and messages answered in seconds — with the same brain, the same calendar, and the same booking rules. No double-bookings between phone and chat.

03

You get the summary, not the noise

Every booking lands in your calendar. Emergencies reach you instantly on WhatsApp or email. Everything else arrives as one clean summary — with the full transcript if you ever want it.

24/7, for real

Nights, weekends, holidays, and the lunch hour when your whole team is with customers.

Books the real calendar

It checks actual availability before offering a slot — so a booking is a booking, not a callback promise.

Emergency triage

A burst pipe, a toothache at midnight, a no-heat call in January — urgency is recognised and escalated to you at once.

Owner alerts

Bookings and urgent cases reach you on WhatsApp or email the moment they happen. Nothing sits in a voicemail box.

For dental practices Booked while the desk was busySample — tomorrow, 8:40 AM

A new patient who hits voicemail at 7 PM books with the practice down the road.

Dental practices

Built for a single practice: one phone number, one calendar, one team to keep informed. It treats a toothache at midnight differently from a cleaning enquiry at noon — because your patients do.

  • Books, reschedules, and cancels into your real calendar — new and returning patients recognised by name.
  • Insurance questions answered from your own list of accepted plans — no guessing, no wrong promises.
  • Emergency triage: pain, swelling, or a broken tooth is flagged and escalated to you immediately.
  • Same voice on messages: a patient who texts instead of calling gets the same answers and the same calendar.

Sample exchange — the way it answers

Patient“Hi — do you take Delta Dental? And is anything open Thursday morning?”

Receptionist“Yes, we accept Delta Dental. Thursday has 9:00 or 10:30 open — shall I hold 9:00 for your checkup?”

HVAC & home services

When the whole crew is on jobs, the phone is the business. The receptionist answers, qualifies, and books around your crew's real capacity — and it knows your service area street by street.

  • Service-area check first — no crew dispatched across town for a job you don't cover.
  • Capacity-aware booking: slots are offered only when a crew can actually take them.
  • Emergency triage: no heat, no cooling, burst pipes — recognised, prioritised, and sent to you at once.
  • Photo intake on messages: customers can send a photo of the unit or the leak, attached to the job.

Saturday, 8:12 AM — WhatsApp

Customer“AC died last night, anyone today?”

Receptionist“Sorry to hear that — you're in our service area and a tech has a 1–3 PM window today. Shall I book it and text you when he's on his way?”

Restaurants

The dinner rush is exactly when orders and reservations arrive — and exactly when nobody can pick up. The receptionist takes both, on the phone and on messages, while your team runs the floor.

  • Orders taken end to end — items, quantities, address, and a clear ticket your kitchen can work from.
  • Table reservations booked against real covers and opening hours — no-shows cut with confirmations.
  • Abandoned-order follow-up: a customer who starts an order and goes quiet gets one polite nudge, 30 minutes later.
  • Menu & hours questions answered from your actual menu — allergens flagged to the kitchen, never guessed.

Friday, 6:58 PM — phone call

Caller“Table for four tonight? And do you do the margherita to go?”

Receptionist“We have 8:15 for four — booked under your name. And yes, I can add a margherita for pickup at 8:00.”

Straight answers

Questions every owner asks first

Can I try it before booking a demo?

Yes — if you're a dental practice, you don't have to imagine anything. The receptionist is live right now on +1 (860) 474-8085. Call it like a patient: ask for a cleaning, check an insurance plan, or describe a toothache, and hear it answer, triage, and book. For other industries, the 15-minute live demo below runs it on your kind of business instead.

Will my customers know it's an AI?

It introduces itself as your business's receptionist and answers in a natural, human pace. What customers actually judge is whether someone competent picked up, understood them, and booked them in — that's the standard it's built and tested against, with you, before launch.

Does it really handle both calls and messages?

Yes — that's the whole point of one front desk. A customer who calls at 9 PM and another who WhatsApps at 9:05 get the same knowledge, the same calendar, and the same booking rules. Nothing gets double-booked between channels.

What happens with an emergency or something it can't handle?

Emergencies are triaged by rules you approve — a dental emergency, a no-heat call, a burst pipe — and escalated to you instantly on WhatsApp or email. Anything outside its knowledge is handed to you with the full transcript, never guessed at.

Do I have to change my phone number?

No. Your existing number forwards to the receptionist — or we set up a dedicated number if you prefer. Either way, your customers dial the number they already know.

How long until it's live?

Per-client setup runs 3–5 working days: knowledge file written and approved by you, calendar connected, then test calls and messages together before the first real customer reaches it.

What does it cost if it doesn't book anything?

The same flat monthly rate — there's no per-booking fee and no percentage of your revenue. That's why the calculator matters: if your missed-call loss is smaller than the plan, we'll tell you on the demo call that you're not ready for it yet.

See it answer a call for your business — live, in 15 minutes.
